'''Robert C. Cahaly''' (born October 16, 1969) is an American [[pollster]] who founded of the [[Trafalgar Group]].  He was a [[political consultant]] for [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican Party]] candidates.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.thetrafalgargroup.org/robert-cahaly-2/|title = Robert Cahaly}}</ref>

Cahaly founded Trafalgar Group in 2016. He drew attention in the aftermath of the election because Trafalgar had was one of a small number of polling firms to predict [[Donald Trump]]'s victory over [[Hillary Clinton]] in the [[2016 presidential election in the united states|2016 presidential election]]. Cahaly stated that Trafalgar's polling methodology was more accurate than other polls because it utilized methods to increase the weighting of  "shy, pro-Trump" voters, which he argued were underrepresented in most polls.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Cahaly|first1=Robert|title=Polling Methodology|url=https://www.thetrafalgargroup.org/polling-methodology/ |accessdate=October 29, 2020 |work=[[Trafalgar Group]] |date=October 29, 2020}}</ref> Cahaly does not disclose Trafalgar's group's methods of polling or its process for ascertaining the volume of shy Trump voters in the electorate.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last1=Russonello |first1=Giovanni |last2=Lyall |first2=Sarah |date=November 8, 2020 |title=The One Pollster in America Who is Sure Trump is Going to Win |url=https://www.nytimes.com/article/trafalgar-group-poll.html |newspaper=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref>

Leading up to the [[2020 United States presidential election|2020 presidential election]], Cahaly garnered substantial media attention for his assertions that Trump would prevail over [[Joe Biden]] in the 2020 election, a claim that contradicted the polling consensus.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{cite web | last = Kaut | first = Kendall | title = Trafalgar's Missed a Lot in 2018 and 2020 | date = November 6, 2020 | url = https://kendallkaut.substack.com/p/trafalgars-missed-a-lot-in-2018-and}}</ref> Cahaly's prediction of a Trump victory proved to be wrong, with him (and Trafalgar) incorrectly predicting Trump victories in five battleground states won by Biden.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2020/11/16/its-important-ask-why-2020-polls-were-off-its-more-important-ask-what-will-happen-next/ |title=It's important to ask why 2020 polls were off. It's more important to ask what will happen next. |date=November 16, 2020 |author1=Philip Bump |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |issn=0190-8286}}</ref>

==Early life==

Cahaly was born in [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]] and grew up in [[Pendleton, South Carolina|Pendleton]], [[South Carolina]], and received a [[Bachelor of Arts]] degree in [[political science]] from the [[University of South Carolina]] in 1995.<ref name="auto"/><ref>{{Cite web |date=November 2, 2010 |title=GOP consultant arrested for illegal "robocalls" |url=https://www.wistv.com/story/13429729/gop-consultant-to-face-sled-arrest-for-illegal-robocalls/ |access-date=November 4, 2024 |website=www.wistv.com |language=en}}</ref> Cahaly is of [[Syrians|Syrian]] heritage and an [[Eastern Orthodox Christian]].<ref name="auto"/><ref>{{Cite web|title=Family tree of Robert CAHALY|url=https://en.geneastar.org/genealogy/cahalyrober/robert-cahaly|access-date=March 27, 2021|website=Geneanet|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Family tree of Margaret Nashawaty|url=https://gw.geneanet.org/tdowling?lang=en&n=nashawaty&oc=0&p=margaret|access-date=March 27, 2021|website=Geneanet|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=The Wellesley Townsman|url=https://wellesley.wickedlocal.com/article/20070329/news/303299820|access-date=March 27, 2021|website=wellesley.wickedlocal.com|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Pogo After Twelve {{!}} News {{!}} The Harvard Crimson|url=https://www.thecrimson.com/article/1953/10/27/pogo-after-twelve-pmichael-cahaly-a/|access-date=March 27, 2021|website=www.thecrimson.com}}</ref> Starting as a child, he volunteered on various political campaigns, before eventually founding his own political consulting firm in 1997.

==Career==
===Political consultant===
Cahaly has worked on campaigns for various Republicans, including governors [[Carroll Campbell]], [[David Beasley]], [[Mike Huckabee]], [[Nikki Haley]], [[Chris Christie]], and [[Henry McMaster]]; US Senators [[Strom Thurmond]], [[Bob Dole]], [[Tim Scott]], and [[Ben Sasse]]; and Presidents [[George H.&nbsp;W. Bush]], [[George W. Bush]], and [[Donald Trump]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Robert Cahaly |url=https://www.thetrafalgargroup.org/robert-cahaly/ |website=[[Trafalgar Group]]}}</ref>{{better source needed|reason=We should not be using the firm's Web site content to verify its claims concerning past clients.|date=November 2020}}

On November 3, 2010, Cahaly was arrested by the [[South Carolina Law Enforcement Division|State Law Enforcement Division]] (SLED) and charged with making illegal [[robocalls]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wistv.com/story/13429729/gop-consultant-to-face-sled-arrest-for-illegal-robocalls|title= GOP consultant arrested for illegal "robocalls"|date= November 2, 2010|accessdate=October 27, 2015}}</ref> Cahaly denied any wrongdoing, stating "It is sad and disappointing that in this charged election cycle full of last minute surprise attacks that Democrat Incumbents and power brokers are leveraging all of their influence to create a last minute salacious headline. We are apparently today's target."  The charges were dismissed in October 2012.<ref>{{cite web |date=October 5, 2012 |title=Charges Against GOP Consultant Cahaly Dropped |url=https://www.postandcourier.com/politics/state_politics/charges-against-gop-consultant-dismissed/article_4e5fdc5e-3a9b-5fce-939d-61329dd7cb22.html |accessdate=October 27, 2015 |website=[[The Post and Courier]]}}</ref> After the charges were dropped, Cahaly filed suit against SLED officials, claiming his constitutional right to free speech had been violated. The subsequent decision of ''[[Cahaly v. LaRosa]]'' found the anti-robocall statute was a content-based restriction on speech and therefore unconstitutional.<ref>{{cite web |title=Fed Court rules law Cahaly charged under unconstitutional |url=https://www.thestate.com/news/politics-government/politics-columns-blogs/the-buzz/article13862843.html |accessdate=October 27, 2015 |website=[[The State (newspaper)|The State]]}}</ref>

===Pollster===
Cahaly gained media attention in 2016 for being one of the few pollsters to accurately predict that [[Donald Trump]] would carry the states of Michigan and Pennsylvania in the [[2016 United States presidential election]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=An Evaluation of 2016 Election Polls in the U.S. - AAPOR|url=https://www.aapor.org/Education-Resources/Reports/An-Evaluation-of-2016-Election-Polls-in-the-U-S.aspx|access-date=November 3, 2020|website=www.aapor.org|archive-date=April 15, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180415063428/https://www.aapor.org/Education-Resources/Reports/An-Evaluation-of-2016-Election-Polls-in-the-U-S.aspx|url-status=dead}}</ref>  Cahaly attributed this partially on the "Shy Trump Voter Theory" that poll respondents are afraid to reveal that they are voting for Trump due to a "[[social desirability bias]]."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kilgore |first=Ed |date=July 29, 2020 |title=There's Still No Evidence Trump Voters Are Particularly 'Shy' |url=https://nymag.com/intelligencer/2020/07/theres-still-no-evidence-trump-voters-are-particularly-shy.html |access-date=November 4, 2024 |website=[[New York (magazine)#Intelligencer|Intelligencer]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=October 9, 2024 |title=Four Problems With 2016 Trump Polling That Could Play Out Again in 2020 - The New York Times |website=[[The New York Times]] |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2019/11/23/us/politics/2020-trump-presidential-polls.html |access-date=November 4, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241009184431/https://www.nytimes.com/2019/11/23/us/politics/2020-trump-presidential-polls.html |archive-date=October 9, 2024 }}</ref>

In November 2020, Cahaly appeared on [[Hannity]] on [[Fox News]] and predicted that Trump would win Pennsylvania, but possibly still lose the state through voter fraud: "He better win by 4 or 5% to make sure he gets victory there. That is the margin he needs to avoid what they will systematically do."<ref>{{cite web |last1=Hall |first1=Colby |title=Trafalgar Pollster Robert Cahaly Makes Baseless Claim: Trump Will Win Pennsylvania, But 'They' Will Steal It With Voter Fraud |url=https://www.mediaite.com/tv/trafalgar-pollster-robert-cahaly-makes-baseless-claim-trump-will-win-pennsylvania-but-they-will-steal-it-with-voter-fraud/ |website=mediaite.com |date=November 2, 2020 |publisher=[[Mediaite]] |accessdate=November 2, 2020 |ref=mediaite}}</ref>

In September 2022, Cahaly, in an interview with Split Ticket, acknowledged methodological changes from his polling of the [[2020 United States elections]].<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Jain |first1=Lakshya |last2=Lee |first2=Michael |last3=Thomas |first3=Armin |last4=Lavelle |first4=Harrison |date=September 20, 2022 |title=What's Going On With Trafalgar's Polls? |url=https://split-ticket.org/2022/09/19/whats-going-on-with-trafalgars-polls/ |access-date=September 20, 2022 |website=[[Split Ticket]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

The [[Trafalgar Group]]'s polling numbers were mostly inaccurate in the [[2022 United States midterm elections]].<ref name="2022Polls">{{Cite web |title=On Polls, Pollsters, and Pundits |url=http://thetartan.org/2022/11/14/pillbox/midterminterview |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221116002509/http://thetartan.org/2022/11/14/pillbox/midterminterview |archive-date=November 16, 2022 |website=[[The Tartan (Carnegie Mellon University)|The Tartan]]}}</ref> Trafalgar's polls incorrectly suggested that Republican candidates such as [[Kari Lake]], [[Mehmet Oz]], [[Tim Michels]], and [[Herschel Walker]], would all win.
